title: The four operations
summary: Add, subtract, multiply and divide with [[integer|integers]], [[negative-number|negative numbers]], decimals and [[fraction|fractions]]. The [[order-of-operations|order of operations]] tells you which part to do first, so every calculation has one right answer.

goals.text: Add, subtract, multiply and divide negative numbers, including temperature changes.
Use the order of operations and brackets to work out a calculation.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals without a calculator.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions and [[mixed-number|mixed numbers]].

before.hint: List multiples of $9$ until $6$ divides one.
before.explain: Multiples of $9$: $9, 18$. $6$ divides $18$. Revise it in {{lesson:1.1}}.

before.prompt: Write $2\frac{3}{7}$ as a single fraction, with no whole-number part.

blocks.text: A [[negative-number|negative number]] is less than zero, like $-5$. On a number line, adding a positive number moves you right (up). Subtracting one moves you left (down).

blocks.alt: Number line from minus 20 to 10. A curved arrow labelled plus 18 jumps from minus 18 up to 0. A second arrow labelled plus 5 jumps from 0 up to 5.
blocks.caption: $-18 + 23 = 5$: up $18$ to reach zero, then $5$ more.

blocks.text: So a freezer at $-18^{\circ}\text{C}$ that warms up by $23^{\circ}\text{C}$ ends at $5^{\circ}\text{C}$.

blocks.statement: Subtracting a negative is adding: $a - (-b) = a + b$. Adding a negative is subtracting: $a + (-b) = a - b$.
blocks.why: Taking away a drop of $b$ degrees leaves it $b$ degrees warmer.

blocks.question: On a mountain it is $-6.4^{\circ}\text{C}$ at dawn and $11.8^{\circ}\text{C}$ at noon. By how much did it rise?

check.hint: Subtracting $-9$ is the same as adding $9$.

blocks.text: To multiply or divide, work out the size, then the sign. Same signs give $+$; different signs give $-$. Anything times $0$ is $0$.

blocks.question: Work out $(-8) \times 3 \div (-6)$.
steps: $\times$ and $\div$ have equal rank, so work left to right.
$24 \div 6 = 4$. The signs are the same, so $-24 \div (-6) = 4$.

blocks.hint: Take two numbers at a time, left to right.

blocks.text: In $2 + 3 \times 4$, adding first gives $20$, but multiplying first gives $14$. So everyone uses the same [[order-of-operations|order of operations]]. The right answer is $14$.

blocks.statement: Brackets first, then Indices (powers and roots), then Division and Multiplication, then Addition and Subtraction. Equal ranks go left to right.

blocks.text: Divide and multiply have equal rank, so go left to right: $12 \div 3 \times 2 = 4 \times 2 = 8$. The same goes for add and subtract: $9 - 4 + 2 = 7$.

blocks.prompt: Which placing of one pair of brackets makes $40 - 7 \times 3 + 2$ equal $5$?
blocks.hint: With no brackets it is $40 - 21 + 2 = 21$. You need to take away more.

blocks.text: A fraction line acts as a bracket: work out the whole top and the whole bottom, then divide. On a calculator, bracket each one.

blocks.question: Use your calculator to work out $\dfrac{4.7 + 3.2^2}{6.1 - 2.45}$. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
steps: Round only at the end, to 3 s.f.

blocks.text: Typing $4.7 + 3.2^2 \div 6.1 - 2.45$ with no brackets. The calculator then divides only $3.2^2$ by $6.1$.
To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points. Fill gaps with zeros: $9.1 = 9.10$.

blocks.hint: Write $9.1$ as $9.10$, then subtract in columns.

blocks.text: To multiply decimals, multiply without the points. Then put back as many decimal places as the two numbers have in total. Drop any end zeros after that: $0.5 \times 0.4 = 0.20 = 0.2$.

blocks.question: Work out $3.4 \times 0.07$.
steps: $3.4$ has $1$ decimal place and $0.07$ has $2$. That makes $3$ in total.
Estimate to check: $3 \times 0.07 = 0.21$, which is close.

blocks.text: To divide by a decimal, multiply both numbers by the same $10$, $100$, … so you divide by a whole number. The answer is unchanged.

blocks.question: Work out $5.16 \div 0.4$.
steps: Short division, keeping the point in place: $51.6 \div 4 = 12.9$.

blocks.text: You can add the tops of [[fraction|fractions]] directly only when the bottoms (denominators) match. Then add the tops (numerators) and keep the bottom: $\frac{2}{9} + \frac{5}{9} = \frac{7}{9}$.
If the bottoms differ, rewrite both over a common denominator. The [[lowest-common-multiple|lowest common multiple]] (LCM) of the bottoms is best.

blocks.question: Work out $\frac{3}{4} + \frac{5}{6}$. Give your answer as a mixed number.
steps: $12$ goes into $19$ once, with $7$ left over.

blocks.text: Adding tops and bottoms: $\frac{3}{4} + \frac{5}{6}$ is not $\frac{8}{10}$. Make the bottoms the same first.

blocks.explain: $\frac{15}{24} - \frac{4}{24} = \frac{11}{24}$. Change the tops as well as the bottoms.

blocks.text: With [[mixed-number|mixed numbers]], change each one to an [[improper-fraction|improper fraction]] first. Then use the same method.

blocks.prompt: A cake uses $1\frac{3}{4}$ cups of flour and its topping $\frac{2}{3}$ of a cup. How many cups in total?
blocks.hint: $1\frac{3}{4} = \frac{7}{4}$. Then use $12$ as the common denominator.

blocks.text: To multiply fractions, multiply the tops and the bottoms. Cancel a top with a bottom first to keep numbers small.

blocks.question: Work out $\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{15}{8}$.
steps: $4$ and $8$ share a factor of $4$: they cancel to $1$ and $2$.
$15$ and $9$ share a factor of $3$: they cancel to $5$ and $3$.

blocks.statement: To divide by a fraction, multiply by its [[reciprocal|reciprocal]]: $\frac{a}{b} \div \frac{c}{d} = \frac{a}{b} \times \frac{d}{c}$, where $b$, $c$ and $d$ are not $0$.
blocks.why: Dividing by $2$ is the same as multiplying by $\frac{1}{2}$. The same works for any fraction.

blocks.text: Only the fraction you divide by turns upside down. Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first.

blocks.question: Work out $2\frac{2}{3} \div 1\frac{1}{9}$. Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
steps: Flip the second fraction and multiply: $\frac{8}{3} \times \frac{9}{10}$.
Cancel: $8$ and $10$ become $4$ and $5$, and $9$ and $3$ become $3$ and $1$.

blocks.text: Dividing the whole numbers and the fractions separately. $2\frac{2}{3} \div 1\frac{1}{9}$ is not $2 \div 1$ with $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{9}$.

blocks.hint: Change both to improper fractions first.

blocks.text: Subtracting a negative is adding: $a - (-b) = a + b$.
Multiply or divide: same signs give $+$, different signs give $-$.
Order: brackets, indices, $\times$ and $\div$, then $+$ and $-$. Equal ranks go left to right. A fraction line acts as a bracket.
Decimals: line up the points to add or subtract; count decimal places to multiply.
Fractions: common denominator to add or subtract. To divide, flip the second and multiply.
Change mixed numbers to improper fractions before you multiply or divide.

mistakes: Flipping the first fraction when you divide. Flip only the one you divide by.
Subtracting tops and bottoms separately: $\frac{5}{8} - \frac{1}{6} \ne \frac{4}{2}$. Use a common denominator.
Multiplying mixed numbers part by part. Use improper fractions.
Getting $5.4$ for the rise from $-6.4$ to $11.8$. It is $11.8 + 6.4 = 18.2$.
examTips: Work out (Papers 1 and 2): show the common denominator or the flipped fraction. That line can earn a method mark.
Give fractions in simplest form, never mixed with decimals like $\frac{1}{0.2}$.
Papers 3 and 4: write down the full display, then round to 3 s.f. unless told otherwise.
